key_insight: Video Streaming Thinking (VST) lets VideoLLMs reason concurrently while they watch video, resolving the latency vs. reasoning-quality trade-off by enabling a synchronized, progressive thinking stream alongside perception.
problem_solved: Existing streaming VideoLLMs focus on perception only and suffer from either delayed logical reasoning (high latency) or reduced answer quality; VST addresses the need for low-latency, continuous reasoning during live video understanding.
method: Introduce a "thinking while watching" paradigm that activates a reasoning stream during video ingestion to produce intermediate hypotheses and early answers.
Decouple and run perception and reasoning as coordinated but asynchronous streams, allowing continuous frame processing and progressive refinement of outputs.
Use adaptive scheduling/progressive refinement to allocate compute and refine early reasoning results into final answers without large test-time scaling-induced delays.
impact: Enables responsive, real-time VideoLLM applications (e.g., live QA, robotics, surveillance) by reducing response latency while preserving reasoning quality, making deployment in interactive settings more practical.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing simultaneous "Watch (frame stream)" and "Think (reasoning stream)" lanes with progressive outputs
Pipeline block diagram of perception stream ↔ reasoning stream with arrows for asynchronous coordination and refinement loop
Latency vs. accuracy trade-off chart comparing naive scaling vs. VST (VST shifts curve toward lower latency for similar accuracy)
Example UI mockup (live video + progressively refined textual responses) to illustrate incremental answers
paper_title: Video Streaming Thinking: VideoLLMs Can Watch and Think Simultaneously
paper_authors: Yiran Guan, Liang Yin, Dingkang Liang, Jianzhong Ju, Zhenbo Luo
